title: git status says every file changed and you touched nothing
summary: Four hundred files modified, an empty diff, and a colleague who cannot reproduce it. Work through the three real causes — file modes, line endings, and assume-unchanged — and fix each one.
mental_model: Git compares the index against the working tree using content, mode and timestamp. A mass 'modified' with no visible diff means one of the non-content fields changed, or the index's cached stat information is stale.

steps.title: Cause one: the executable bit
steps.why: Copying files through a Windows share, a zip, or some Docker mounts loses the executable bit. Git tracks that bit as part of the index entry, so the file counts as modified with no content change at all. Here we change it directly in the index with --chmod, which behaves identically on every platform (on Windows, core.fileMode defaults to false, so a real chmod would show nothing).
steps.expect: Two files modified, an empty content diff, and `--summary` showing the mode change 100755 => 100644.

verify.label: the modification is a mode change, not content
…and not a single line of content changed
verify.hint: the diff header shows old mode / new mode and nothing else

steps.title: Fix it properly, or ignore it
steps.why: Restoring the bit is the correct fix. `core.fileMode false` tells git to stop tracking the bit at all — right on Windows, wrong on a Unix machine where a lost bit really does break the deploy.
commands: sh -c 'git config core.fileMode || echo "core.fileMode not set (defaults to false on Windows)"'
steps.expect: Clean again, with the bit restored rather than the check disabled.

verify.label: the mode change is resolved
verify.hint: chmod +x the scripts, or set core.fileMode false if you are on Windows

steps.title: Cause two: line endings
steps.why: An editor saved every file with CRLF. Every line differs at the byte level, so every file is modified — and `git diff` shows entire files rewritten, which looks like catastrophe.

actions.run: sh -c 'for f in src/app.py src/pump.py config.ini; do sed -i "s/$/\r/" "$f"; done'

steps.expect: Three files modified; ignoring carriage returns shows zero real changes.

verify.label: line endings alone made every file look modified

steps.title: Prove it is only line endings, then fix it at the repo level
steps.why: `--ignore-cr-at-eol` proving an empty diff is the diagnosis. `.gitattributes` with `text=auto` plus a renormalise is the cure, and it binds everyone rather than only your machine.
steps.expect: Clean tree, and the index storing LF regardless of what the editor writes.

verify.label: the repository stores LF, so editor choice no longer matters

steps.title: Cause three: a file that refuses to update
steps.why: The opposite symptom, same family. `assume-unchanged` tells git to stop checking a file — usually set years ago to ignore local config edits. The file then never appears modified, and your changes silently never get committed.
steps.expect: Status is clean despite a real edit, and ls-files -v shows a lowercase flag marking the file.

verify.label: one file is marked assume-unchanged and invisible to status

steps.title: Undo it and commit the change that was being swallowed
steps.why: `--no-assume-unchanged` restores normal behaviour and the edit reappears immediately. This flag has cost more people more hours than almost anything else in git.
commands: git commit -q -m "Raise the tank temperature threshold"

verify.label: no file is hidden from status any more
the previously swallowed edit is committed

steps.title: The harmless fourth cause
steps.why: Sometimes the index's cached stat data is simply stale — after restoring a backup, or a clock jump. `update-index --refresh` re-checks content and quietly drops files whose content is unchanged.
steps.expect: Nothing modified: touching a file changes its timestamp, and git falls back to comparing content.

verify.label: the working tree is clean and honest again
verify.hint: fix the mode bits, normalise line endings, clear assume-unchanged

verify.label: line endings are normalised in the repository
no file is hidden by assume-unchanged
the edit that was being swallowed is committed
the executable bit is intact in the index

pitfalls: `git diff --summary` reveals mode changes that `git diff` hides. It is the first thing to run when status and diff disagree.
`core.fileMode false` is right on Windows and dangerous on Unix — it stops git noticing a script that lost its executable bit.
`--assume-unchanged` is a performance hint, not an ignore mechanism. Git may still notice the file, and your changes may vanish. Use a separate untracked config file instead.
`--skip-worktree` is the slightly safer sibling, and is what sparse-checkout uses. Both hide files from status.
`git ls-files -v` prints a lowercase letter for any file flagged this way. Run it whenever a file mysteriously refuses to change.
cheatsheet: mode changes, renames, new and deleted files
prove a diff is only line endings
files hidden by assume-unchanged or skip-worktree
drop stale stat data from the index
